<!-- Generated by `cargo run -p xtask -- gen-settings` from xtask/src/settings.rs. Edit that, not this. -->

oxtel reads the standard OpenTelemetry variables, and a few of its own that start with `OXTEL_`, so the people who run a program can change what it records and where it goes without a rebuild. A program can also make most of these choices in code, with `oxtel::builder()`; its documentation says which ones the environment overrides.

oxtel follows the specification's variables and defaults with one deliberate exception: the specification sends to `localhost:4318` even when nothing is set, and oxtel sends nothing until an endpoint is set or an exporter is named.

## Turning things on and off

Nothing is sent anywhere until an endpoint is set or an exporter is named. Local log lines are on from the start.

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_SDK_DISABLED`</span> | `false` | `true` turns off traces, metrics and logs, and leaves only local log lines. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER`</span> | `otlp` once an endpoint is set, otherwise `none` | Where spans go: `otlp`, `console` (readable lines on standard output) or `none`. Several can be listed, separated by commas. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER`</span> | `otlp` once an endpoint is set, otherwise `none` | Where metrics go: `otlp`, `prometheus` (a `/metrics` endpoint, at the host and port below), `console` or `none`. Several can be listed, separated by commas. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`</span> | `otlp` once an endpoint is set, otherwise `none` | Where log records go: `otlp`, `console` or `none`. Local log lines are separate: see `OXTEL_LOG_FORMAT`. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_CONFIG_FILE`</span> | unset | A declarative configuration file (schema 1.x) to build every pipeline from, instead of these variables, which the file can still substitute with `${NAME}`. Needs oxtel's `config` feature, which is on by default. A file that can't be read is an error. |

## Local log lines

What oxtel writes to the program's own output, separately from what it exports.

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`RUST_LOG`</span> | `info` | How much is recorded, as directives such as `info` or `info,hyper=warn`. It applies to spans and exported log records too, unless the program sets their filters in code. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OXTEL_LOG_FORMAT`</span> | `auto` | How local log lines look: `auto` (text on a terminal, JSON otherwise), `text`, `json` (flat, with OpenTelemetry field names), `ecs` (Elastic Common Schema) or `none`. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OXTEL_LOG_OUTPUT`</span> | `stderr` | Where local log lines go: `stderr` or `stdout`. Standard output is left alone by default, since it carries a command-line tool's results and an MCP stdio server's protocol. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OXTEL_MAPPINGS`</span> | `all` | `none` turns off the spans and metrics oxtel makes from what libraries already log, such as sqlx's queries. |

## Your service

What every span, metric and log record says about where it came from.

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`</span> | `unknown_service:` and the executable's name | The service's name, as backends show it. It takes precedence over a `service.name` in `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`</span> | unset | More about the service, as `key=value` pairs separated by commas, such as `deployment.environment.name=prod`. They take precedence over what's detected. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_EXPERIMENTAL_RESOURCE_DETECTORS`</span> | all of them | Which detectors run at startup, separated by commas: `service`, `host`, `os`, `process`, `container` and `k8s`; or `none`. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`K8S_NODE_NAME`</span> | unset | The Kubernetes node, for `k8s.node.name`. Pass it into the pod through the downward API, from `spec.nodeName`. The namespace and pod are found without it. |

## Sending with OTLP

Where and how OTLP exporters send. Each of these is also read for one signal, with `TRACES_`, `METRICS_` or `LOGS_` after `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_`, and that one takes precedence.

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`</span> | unset: nothing is sent. With an exporter named, `http://localhost:4318`, or `http://localhost:4317` for gRPC | Where to send. Over HTTP, oxtel adds `/v1/traces`, `/v1/metrics` or `/v1/logs`; a signal's own endpoint is used as it is, so it needs the full path. Over gRPC, it's used as it is. Also per signal, such as `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT`. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL`</span> | `http/protobuf` | `http/protobuf`, `http/json`, or `grpc` with oxtel's `grpc` feature. Without the feature, `grpc` falls back to `http/protobuf` with a warning. Also per signal, such as `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL`. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`</span> | unset | Headers to send, as `key=value` pairs separated by commas, such as `Authorization=Bearer <token>`. Values may be percent-encoded. Over gRPC they're sent as metadata. A signal's own headers are added to these, replacing any of the same name. Also per signal, such as `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_HEADERS`. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_COMPRESSION`</span> | none | `gzip` compresses what's sent. Also per signal, such as `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_COMPRESSION`. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT`</span> | `10000` | How long each export may take, in milliseconds. Also per signal, such as `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_TIMEOUT`. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE`</span> | the bundled root certificates | A PEM file of the certificates to verify the receiver with, in place of the bundled roots. Also per signal, such as `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_CERTIFICATE`. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE`</span> | unset | A PEM file with a client certificate to present, for mutual TLS. It needs the key below. Also per signal, such as `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE`. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CLIENT_KEY`</span> | unset | A PEM file with the client certificate's private key. Also per signal, such as `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_CLIENT_KEY`. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_TEMPORALITY_PREFERENCE`</span> | `cumulative` | `delta` (or `lowmemory`, the same for oxtel) makes OTLP's counters and histograms report the change since the previous export. Other exporters keep their totals. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_DEFAULT_HISTOGRAM_AGGREGATION`</span> | `explicit_bucket_histogram` | `base2_exponential_bucket_histogram` makes OTLP's histograms exponential. Prometheus scrapes are unchanged. |

## Prometheus

The built-in `/metrics` endpoint, served with `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=prometheus`.

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_EXPORTER_PROMETHEUS_HOST`</span> | `localhost` | The address to listen on. `0.0.0.0` listens on every interface, as a scraper outside a container needs. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_EXPORTER_PROMETHEUS_PORT`</span> | `9464` | The port to listen on. |

## Sampling and propagation

Which traces are kept, and how a trace crosses from one service to the next.

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER`</span> | `parentbased_always_on` | `always_on`, `always_off`, `traceidratio`, `parentbased_always_on`, `parentbased_always_off` or `parentbased_traceidratio`. The `parentbased_` ones follow the caller's decision when there is one. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG`</span> | `1.0` | For the ratio samplers, the share of traces to keep, from 0 to 1. A ratio that isn't one means 1.0. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_PROPAGATORS`</span> | `tracecontext,baggage` | How trace context travels between services: `tracecontext` (W3C), `baggage` or `none`. Others are warned about and ignored. |

## Batching and export intervals

When spans, log records and metrics are sent. Times are in milliseconds.

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY`</span> | `5000` | How often a batch of spans is sent. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_BSP_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE`</span> | `2048` | How many spans wait to be sent. Beyond it, new spans are dropped and counted, rather than slowing the program. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_BSP_MAX_EXPORT_BATCH_SIZE`</span> | `512` | The most spans sent at once. It can't exceed the queue. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_BSP_EXPORT_TIMEOUT`</span> | `30000` | How long sending a batch of spans may take. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_BLRP_SCHEDULE_DELAY`</span> | `1000` | How often a batch of log records is sent. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_BLRP_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE`</span> | `2048` | How many log records wait to be sent. Beyond it, new ones are dropped and counted. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_BLRP_MAX_EXPORT_BATCH_SIZE`</span> | `512` | The most log records sent at once. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_BLRP_EXPORT_TIMEOUT`</span> | `30000` | How long sending a batch of log records may take. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL`</span> | `60000` | How often metrics are pushed. Prometheus scrapes whenever it likes. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_TIMEOUT`</span> | `30000` | How long pushing metrics may take. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_METRICS_EXEMPLAR_FILTER`</span> | `trace_based` | Which measurements keep the trace and span ids of the span they were made in: `trace_based` (those in a sampled span), `always_on` or `always_off`. |

## Limits

Caps that keep one runaway span or record from using unbounded memory. What's over a limit is dropped.

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_ATTRIBUTE_COUNT_LIMIT`</span> | `128` | The most attributes on a span or log record, unless the more specific limits below say otherwise. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_SPAN_ATTRIBUTE_COUNT_LIMIT`</span> | `128` | The most attributes on a span. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_SPAN_EVENT_COUNT_LIMIT`</span> | `128` | The most events on a span. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_SPAN_LINK_COUNT_LIMIT`</span> | `128` | The most links on a span. |
| <span data-pagefind-weight="7">`OTEL_LOGRECORD_ATTRIBUTE_COUNT_LIMIT`</span> | `128` | The most attributes on a log record. |

## How this page is kept true

It's generated from a table in the repository's `xtask`, which CI checks against the code on every change: every `OTEL_` or `OXTEL_` name the code reads has to be in the table, and every setting in the table has to be read where the table says. A setting can't be added, renamed or dropped without this page following.
